records.source: וַיְהִ֡י בְּיוֹם֩ כַּלּ֨וֹת מֹשֶׁ֜ה לְהָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ן וַיִּמְשַׁ֨ח אֹת֜וֹ וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וַיִּמְשָׁחֵ֖ם וַיְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was on [the] day of finishing Moses to set up the tabernacle, and he anointed it and consecrated it and all its articles, and the altar and all its articles, and he anointed them and consecrated them,
pieces: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, when he had anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, and had anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils,

L.1: And it came about on the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, and anointed it and consecrated it and all its articles, and the altar and all its articles, and anointed them and consecrated them,

R.1: Moses finished setting up the tabernacle. He anointed it with oil and set it apart for God, together with everything used in it. He did the same for the altar and all the things used with it.

decisions.choice: a time clause that runs on into verse 2: on the day Moses finished ..., the leaders brought offerings
decisions.reason: The verse opens with "and it came about on the day" and lists what Moses did that day; the main statement, the leaders' gifts, comes in verse 2. "On the day" can mean "at the time when" (Genesis 2:4): the leaders' offerings for the altar were spread over twelve days (verses 11-83).

decisions.choice: the day the tabernacle was set up: the first day of the first month of the second year
decisions.reason: Exodus 40:17-33 tells of this day, and Exodus 40:9-11 and Leviticus 8:10-11 of the anointing. It was a month before the census that opens the book, which began on the first day of the second month (1:1). The chapter goes back in time to tell what the leaders gave when the tabernacle was first set up.

decisions.choice: anointed and consecrated: smeared with the holy oil and so made holy, set apart for God's use
decisions.reason: The anointing oil was made for this purpose (Exodus 30:22-29). Whatever it touched became holy and could be used only in God's service.

decisions.choice: anointed it with oil and set it apart for God
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing used and what consecrating means, and keeps verse 1 as sentences of its own. It ties the two verses together with "On that day" in verse 2.

records.heading: Offerings for the dedication of the altar

records.source: וַיַּקְרִ֨יבוּ֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם הֵ֚ם נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַמַּטֹּ֔ת הֵ֥ם הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עַל־הַפְּקֻדִֽים׃
records.gloss: and brought near [the] leaders of Israel, heads of [the] house of their fathers; they [were the] leaders of the tribes, they [were] the ones standing over the counted [ones].
pieces: the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral families, brought offerings. They were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had been in charge of those who were counted.

L.2: and the leaders of Israel, the heads of the house of their fathers, brought [offerings]; they [were] the leaders of the tribes, they [were] the ones standing over those counted.

R.2: On that day the leaders of Israel brought offerings. They were the heads of the families and the leaders of the tribes. They had been in charge of counting the people.

decisions.choice: brought near: brought offerings, without an object here
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for presenting an offering at the sanctuary (Leviticus 1:2). It has no object in this verse; verse 3 says what the leaders brought.

decisions.choice: the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral families: the twelve tribal leaders
decisions.reason: These are the men named in 1:5-16, one from each tribe, who helped Moses and Aaron with the census. A "house of fathers" is a family traced through the father's line, the unit by which the tribes were counted (1:2).

decisions.choice: standing over those counted: in charge of the census
decisions.reason: To "stand over" a group is to have charge of it. "Those counted" are the men registered in the census of chapter 1 (1:44).

decisions.choice: On that day
decisions.reason: Verse 2 completes the time clause of verse 1. Readable, which ends verse 1 with a full stop, adds "On that day" to keep the link.

records.source: וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־קָרְבָּנָ֜ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה שֵׁשׁ־עֶגְלֹ֥ת צָב֙ וּשְׁנֵ֣י עָשָׂ֣ר בָּקָ֔ר עֲגָלָ֛ה עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂאִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וֹר לְאֶחָ֑ד וַיַּקְרִ֥יבוּ אוֹתָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they brought their offering before Yahweh, six carts of covering and two [and] ten oxen, a cart for two of the leaders and an ox for one, and they brought them near before the tabernacle.
pieces: They brought their offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: six covered carts and twelve oxen, one cart for every two leaders and an ox from each one. They presented them in front of the tabernacle.

L.3: And they brought their offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, six covered carts and twelve oxen, a cart for [every] two of the leaders and an ox for each one; and they presented them before the tabernacle.

R.3: They brought their offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: six carts with covers and twelve oxen. Each pair of leaders gave one cart, and each leader gave one ox. They brought these to the front of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: carts of covering: covered carts
alternatives: wagons of a particular kind, or litters
decisions.reason: The word with "carts" is rare. It is usually taken to mean a cover or roof, carts with a covering to protect the load. Isaiah 66:20 uses the same word in a list of ways to travel, which has led some to think of a kind of litter or wagon.

decisions.choice: a cart for two of the leaders and an ox for each one: the twelve leaders shared the six carts, two to a cart, and each gave one ox
decisions.reason: Six carts and twelve oxen is one pair of oxen to pull each cart, given by the twelve leaders together.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: at the sanctuary where the LORD was present
decisions.reason: "Before the LORD" here means at the tabernacle, as the end of the verse says. A gift brought there was a gift to God himself, before it was handed to the Levites (verses 5-6).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶריְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer to a gift no one had asked for
decisions.reason: The leaders brought the carts and oxen of their own accord (verse 3). The LORD now tells Moses to accept them and what they are for (verse 5).

records.source: קַ֚ח מֵֽאִתָּ֔ם וְהָי֕וּ לַעֲבֹ֕ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֥י עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Take from them, and they will be for serving the service of [the] tent of meeting, and you will give them to the Levites, a man according to [the] mouth of his service.
pieces: "Accept these from them, so that they may be used for the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each as his work requires."

L.5: "Take [them] from them, and they shall be for doing the service of the tent of meeting; and you shall give them to the Levites, each one according to his service."

R.5: "Accept these gifts from them. They are to be used for the work of the meeting tent. Give them to the Levites, to each group as it needs them for its work."

decisions.choice: the service of the tent of meeting: the Levites' work of taking down, carrying and setting up the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Chapter 4 gives each Levite clan its share of this work on the march (4:1-33). The carts and oxen were for moving the tent and its parts.

decisions.choice: each according to the mouth of his service: to each as his work requires
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of" means "in the measure of" or "as ... requires". Verses 7-9 show what this meant: each clan received carts by the size of its load.

decisions.choice: according to his service
decisions.reason: Literal leaves out "the mouth of", which in this phrase means only "as much as"; the idiom is explained in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: to each group
decisions.reason: "Each one" here means each part of the Levites, which received carts clan by clan (verses 7-8). Readable says "group" so that the gifts are not thought of as given to every single Levite.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־הָעֲגָלֹ֖ת וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֑ר וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אוֹתָ֖ם אֶל־הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And took Moses the carts and the oxen, and he gave them to the Levites.
pieces: So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.

L.6: And Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.

R.6: So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.

decisions.choice: Moses does as he was told
decisions.reason: The two verbs answer the two commands of verse 5: "take" and "give". Verses 7-9 say how he divided the gifts.

records.source: אֵ֣ת׀שְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֲגָלֹ֗ת וְאֵת֙ אַרְבַּ֣עַת הַבָּקָ֔ר נָתַ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁ֑וֹן כְּפִ֖י עֲבֹדָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Two of the carts and four of the oxen he gave to [the] sons of Gershon, according to [the] mouth of their service.
pieces: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work required.

L.7: Two carts and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.

R.7: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Levites of Gershon's family, because they needed them for their work.

decisions.choice: the sons of Gershon: the Levite clans that carried the tent's fabrics
decisions.reason: The Gershonites carried the curtains of the tabernacle, its coverings, the screens and the hangings of the courtyard (4:24-26). Their load was lighter than Merari's, so they received half as many carts (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the Gershonites / the Levites of Gershon's family
decisions.reason: "Sons of Gershon" names a group of clans descended from Gershon, son of Levi (3:17-21), not his own sons. Literal keeps "sons of".

records.source: וְאֵ֣ת׀אַרְבַּ֣ע הָעֲגָלֹ֗ת וְאֵת֙ שְׁמֹנַ֣ת הַבָּקָ֔ר נָתַ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֑י כְּפִי֙ עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם בְּיַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And four of the carts and eight of the oxen he gave to [the] sons of Merari, according to [the] mouth of their service, by [the] hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
pieces: And he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work required. They were under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

L.8: And four carts and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

R.8: He gave four carts and eight oxen to the Levites of Merari's family, because they needed them for their work. Ithamar son of Aaron the priest was in charge of them.

decisions.choice: the sons of Merari: the Levite clans that carried the tent's frame
decisions.reason: The Merarites carried the frames, bars, posts and bases of the tabernacle and its courtyard, with their pegs and cords (4:31-32), the heaviest load, so they received twice as many carts as the Gershonites.

decisions.choice: under the hand of Ithamar: under his direction
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means under someone's charge. Ithamar the priest oversaw the work of both the Gershonites and the Merarites (4:28, 33), so the phrase may cover verse 7 as well as this verse.

decisions.choice: the Merarites / the Levites of Merari's family
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "sons of Merari" names the clans descended from Merari, son of Levi (3:20, 33).

records.source: וְלִבְנֵ֥י קְהָ֖ת לֹ֣א נָתָ֑ן כִּֽי־עֲבֹדַ֤ת הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ עֲלֵהֶ֔ם בַּכָּתֵ֖ף יִשָּֽׂאוּ׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of Kohath he did not give, because the service of the holy [things was] on them; on the shoulder they would carry.
pieces: But he gave none to the Kohathites, because they were responsible for the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.

L.9: But to the sons of Kohath he did not give [any], because the service of the holy [things was] on them; on the shoulder they carried [them].

R.9: But he did not give any carts to the Levites of Kohath's family. Their work was to take care of the holy things, and they had to carry them on their shoulders.

decisions.choice: the Kohathites carried the holy things on their shoulders, not on carts
decisions.reason: The Kohathites carried the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars and the holy utensils, wrapped by the priests and carried on poles (4:4-15). When the ark was later moved on a new cart, the outcome was disaster (2 Samuel 6:3-7), and David then had the Levites carry it on their shoulders "as Moses commanded" (1 Chronicles 15:13-15).

decisions.choice: the service of the holy things was on them: it was their duty
decisions.reason: "Was on them" means it was their task. The verb "carry" is in a form that describes what they did regularly, each time the camp moved.

decisions.choice: gave none / did not give any carts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he did not give". Balanced and Readable supply what was not given.

records.source: וַיַּקְרִ֣יבוּ הַנְּשִׂאִ֗ים אֵ֚ת חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּי֖וֹם הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּקְרִ֧יבוּ הַנְּשִׂיאִ֛ם אֶת־קָרְבָּנָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And brought near the leaders the dedication of the altar on [the] day of anointing it, and brought near the leaders their offering before the altar.
pieces: The leaders also brought offerings for the dedication of the altar at the time it was anointed. They presented their offerings in front of the altar.

L.10: And the leaders presented the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed; and the leaders presented their offering before the altar.

R.10: The leaders also brought offerings to dedicate the altar at the time it was anointed. They placed their offerings in front of the altar.

decisions.choice: the dedication of the altar: the gifts that marked the altar's first use
decisions.reason: The word means a dedication or opening, the start of something's use. It is used again for the dedication of Solomon's altar (2 Chronicles 7:9) and of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 12:27). Here it names both the event and the offerings brought for it (verses 84, 88).

decisions.choice: on the day it was anointed: at the time it was anointed
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "on the day" sets the time in general: verse 11 spreads the gifts over twelve days, and verse 88 says they came "after it was anointed".

decisions.choice: brought offerings for the dedication
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "presented the dedication". Balanced and Readable say what was presented, offerings for the dedication.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד לַיּ֗וֹם נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לַיּ֔וֹם יַקְרִ֨יבוּ֙ אֶת־קָרְבָּנָ֔ם לַחֲנֻכַּ֖ת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃ס
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, leader one for the day, leader one for the day, they will bring near their offering for [the] dedication of the altar.
pieces: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "They are to present their offerings for the dedication of the altar one leader each day."

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "One leader for the day, one leader for the day, they shall present their offering for the dedication of the altar."

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Each leader is to bring his offering for the dedication of the altar on a day of his own, one leader each day."

decisions.choice: one leader for the day, one leader for the day: one leader each day
decisions.reason: Saying a phrase twice gives it the sense "each" or "one after another". The leaders came one at a time, on twelve days in a row (verses 12-83).

decisions.choice: they shall present their offering: each leader his own
decisions.reason: "They" are the twelve leaders, and "their offering" is the gift of each in turn. Verses 12-83 show that every leader brought exactly the same offering.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י הַמַּקְרִ֛יב בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן אֶת־קָרְבָּנ֑וֹ נַחְשׁ֥וֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָ֖ב לְמַטֵּ֥ה יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was the one bringing near on the day the first his offering Nahshon son of Amminadab, of [the] tribe of Judah.
pieces: The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah.

L.12: And the one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.

R.12: On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab brought his offering. He was from the tribe of Judah.

decisions.choice: Judah first: the order of the camp
decisions.reason: The tribes come in the order of the camp in chapter 2: Judah, Issachar and Zebulun on the east, then Reuben, Simeon and Gad, then Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin, then Dan, Asher and Naphtali (2:3-31). Judah's camp led the march (2:9; 10:14).

decisions.choice: Nahshon son of Amminadab: the leader of Judah
decisions.reason: He is named as Judah's leader in 1:7 and 2:3. His sister Elisheba was Aaron's wife (Exodus 6:23), and he is an ancestor of David (Ruth 4:20-22).

decisions.choice: the one who presented his offering: the opening of the first of twelve matching reports
decisions.reason: The first report is introduced more fully than the rest. From verse 18 on, each report opens only with the day, the leader and his tribe.

records.heading: The offerings of the twelve leaders, day by day

records.source: וְקָרְבָּנ֞וֹ קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּמֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָהּ֒ מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם׀מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לְמִנְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And his offering [was] dish of silver one, thirty and a hundred its weight, basin one [of] silver, seventy shekel[s] by [the] shekel of the holy [place], both of them full [of] fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering,
pieces: His offering was one silver dish weighing {{units:about 3 1/4 pounds|130 shekels}} and one silver basin weighing {{units:about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard|seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel}}, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering,

L.13: And his offering [was] one silver dish, its weight [was] 130 [shekels], one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering,

R.13: His offering was a silver plate that weighed {{units:about 3 1/4 pounds|130 shekels}} and a silver bowl that weighed {{units:about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard|seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel}}. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil, for a grain offering.

decisions.choice: a dish and a basin: vessels for the altar's use
decisions.reason: The dish is the kind of wide plate made for the table of the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:29). The basin is the bowl used for the blood of the offerings, which was splashed against the altar (Exodus 27:3; 24:6). The vessels themselves were part of the gift.

decisions.choice: 130 and seventy shekels by the sanctuary shekel: weights of silver
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight of about 11.5 grams, or two-fifths of an ounce. "Shekels" is said only once, after "seventy", but the first number is a weight in shekels too (verse 85). The sanctuary shekel was the official standard for things given to the sanctuary (Exodus 30:13), and it covers both weights.

decisions.choice: full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering
decisions.reason: The vessels came filled with a grain offering of the kind set out in Leviticus 2:1-5: fine flour with olive oil, part of it burned on the altar and the rest given to the priests (Leviticus 2:2-3).

decisions.choice: about 3 1/4 pounds / about 1 3/4 pounds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weights in modern measures, rounded, with the shekels as the setting's alternative. Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: plate / bowl
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the two vessels. Literal and Balanced keep "dish" and "basin", as in Exodus 25:29 and 27:3.

records.source: כַּ֥ף אַחַ֛ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מְלֵאָ֥ה קְטֹֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: pan one [of] ten [shekels of] gold, full [of] incense,
pieces: one gold pan weighing {{units:about 4 ounces|ten shekels}}, full of incense,

L.14: one pan of ten [shekels of] gold, full of incense,

R.14: He also gave a small gold pan that weighed {{units:about 4 ounces|ten shekels}}. It was full of incense.

decisions.choice: a pan full of incense: a small dish for the incense burned in the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the palm of the hand, and so a small, shallow dish shaped like it. Such pans were made for the table in the holy place (Exodus 25:29). The incense was burned on the golden altar (Exodus 30:1-8).

decisions.choice: ten gold: ten shekels' weight of gold
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the number and the metal. Verse 86 confirms that this is a weight in shekels by the sanctuary standard, about 115 grams.

decisions.choice: He also gave
decisions.reason: The list of verses 13-17 is one long sentence. Readable breaks it into short sentences and supplies "He gave" to start each one.

records.source: פַּ֣ר אֶחָ֞ד בֶּן־בָּקָ֗ר אַ֧יִל אֶחָ֛ד כֶּֽבֶשׂ־אֶחָ֥ד בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖וֹ לְעֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: bull one, son of [the] herd, ram one, lamb one, son of its year, for a burnt offering,
pieces: one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,

L.15: one bull, a young one of the herd, one ram, one male lamb, a son of its year, for a burnt offering,

decisions.reason: This points back to the fine flour in the dishes and basins (verse 13). Grain offerings often went with burnt offerings (Numbers 15:1-12).

decisions.reason: These are twelve times the peace offerings of verse 17: two oxen and five each of rams, male goats and lambs. The "oxen" of the single lists are counted here as bulls.

records.gloss: And when went Moses into [the] tent of meeting to speak with him, and he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat which [was] on [the] ark of the testimony, from between [the] two cherubim; and he spoke to him.
pieces: When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to him.

L.89: And when Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that [was] on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to him.

R.89: When Moses went into the meeting tent to talk with God, he heard the voice speaking to him. It came from above the lid of the ark that holds the covenant tablets, from between the two cherubim. That is how God spoke with Moses.

decisions.choice: the voice from between the cherubim: the promise of Exodus 25:22 kept
decisions.reason: The LORD had said he would meet Moses and speak with him from above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim on the ark (Exodus 25:22). Now that the tabernacle is set up and dedicated, it happens.

decisions.choice: when Moses went in: the event, which may also describe what happened each time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the scene with "and when Moses went". It may tell of one occasion, or of what happened whenever Moses went in (compare Exodus 33:7-11). Both fit the verse.

decisions.choice: the voice speaking to him
decisions.reason: The verb form for "speaking" is unusual, one that can mean speaking to oneself or conversing. It stresses that Moses heard the voice itself speaking to him, not a vision. "Him" in "to speak with him" and "he spoke to him" is the LORD, last named in verse 11.

decisions.choice: the mercy seat: the gold cover of the ark
decisions.reason: The word is linked to the verb for making atonement. Blood was sprinkled on it on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:14-15). The cherubim, winged heavenly creatures of gold, stood at its two ends (Exodus 25:17-21).

decisions.choice: to talk with God / That is how God spoke with Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "him". Readable names God and Moses so that the reader can follow who is speaking to whom.

decisions.choice: the lid of the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable describes the mercy seat and the ark of the testimony in plain words, as in Exodus 25:17-22.
